clue.text: Jerseys, perhaps, raised in particular place

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising something lifts it so it reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a jersey is one example of a top, a garment for the upper body

explanation.surface: Jersey cows, perhaps, being bred in one particular part of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerseys look like the cattle breed from the Channel Islands, but here they are woolly jumpers, examples of tops; written upwards they give SPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a noun for a specific location, as in a quiet spot by the river.

clue.text: Eccentricity of Foreign Office manual lacking introduction

indicators.note: to lack an introduction is to be without an opening, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: FO is the standard abbreviation for the Foreign Office
a bible is an authoritative handbook, as in the gardener's bible

explanation.surface: A Whitehall rulebook so quirky that it starts without an introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: A bible in the loose sense is any definitive handbook on a subject, like a cook's bible, which is why it can stand for a manual.
explanation.definitionFit: A foible is a small personal quirk or oddity of character, close to a minor eccentricity.

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so this piece is placed behind the other

blocks.note: a stag is a male deer, and a stag party is men only
an element of a situation is a factor in it

explanation.surface: A rowdy criminal element trailing along behind a stag party.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that stag is being used loosely: a stag is a male deer, and stag nights are male gatherings.
explanation.definitionFit: A malefactor is a formal word for a wrongdoer or lawbreaker, a straightforward synonym for a criminal.

clue.text: Oddly mean bloodsuckers getting bad blood

indicators.note: oddly points to the odd-numbered positions, so only the first and third letters are kept

blocks.note: letters one and three of the word
lice are parasites that feed on blood

explanation.surface: Nasty parasitic insects stirring up resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: Mean looks like an adjective describing the bloodsuckers, but only its odd letters are wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad blood is an idiom for ill feeling or enmity between people, which is what malice means.

indicators.note: in a down entry, upsetting tips something over so it reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: jet is a black gemstone
taken as written
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: Throw that stone away, it has upset the child.
explanation.walkthrough: Jet is fossilised wood polished as a black gem, a common crossword stone; only the little word between flips.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw overboard or get rid of something unwanted, a synonym for discarding it.

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words that follow, running across them

blocks.note: the end of the town name joined to the start of the next word

explanation.surface: Passing time somewhere around the town of Ross-on-Wye.
explanation.walkthrough: Ross-on-Wye is a market town in Herefordshire on the River Wye; the place name is just a carrier for the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is a fixed span of time, twelve months long, so it is one example of a period of time.

clue.text: Appliances without charge and almost nothing showing at first

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
at first means only the opening letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: something without charge costs nothing
zero is nothing
the opening letter

explanation.surface: Kitchen appliances given away free with almost nothing on display.
explanation.walkthrough: Zero is shortened to ZER and the first letter of showing completes the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Freezers are domestic machines for keeping food frozen, so they are examples of household appliances.

indicators.note: into means going inside something, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: a net is used to trap animals
X is the classic algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Tracking a mysterious stranger into an ambush.
explanation.walkthrough: Mathematicians call an unknown quantity x, a convention crosswords use constantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Next as an adjective describes what comes immediately after, as in the following day or the next day.

blocks.note: to prop is to hold up or support
agate is a banded semi-precious stone

explanation.surface: Someone passing over a stone that holds something up.
explanation.walkthrough: Pass on reads like a polite refusal, but it means to spread or transmit, as ideas or genes are passed on.
explanation.definitionFit: To propagate a belief or a plant is to spread it and transmit it further, which is passing it on.

clue.text: Weird and revolting rage suppressed by drugs

indicators.note: revolting means turning over, so these letters go back to front
suppressed means held down and enclosed, so this piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: ire is anger or rage
E is slang for ecstasy, so two of them are drugs

explanation.surface: A strange, disgusting fit of anger kept in check by medication.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolting looks like an adjective meaning disgusting but works as a turning-over signal; E for ecstasy is a crossword staple, doubled for the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie describes something strange and unsettling, uncanny in a frightening way, a close synonym of weird.

blocks.note: first meaning: to put forward a motion for discussion
second meaning: the fare served
third meaning: a timetable or chart of figures

explanation.walkthrough: Food schedule looks like a meal plan, but each word is a separate meaning, making three senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: In British meetings you table a motion by proposing it; a table is also the food provided and a chart or timetable.

blocks.note: to inter is to bury a body
a sect is a religious or political group

explanation.surface: A burial carried out by a group with a cross on the grave.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like it might be the Lancashire town, but it is a verb; cross is the definition, not a crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines or roads that intersect meet and pass over each other, which is crossing.

clue.text: Work in empty theatre following musical drama

indicators.note: an empty word has had its middle removed, leaving only its outer letters
following means coming after, so this piece is placed behind the other

blocks.note: an opera is a drama set to music
just the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Getting a job in a deserted theatre after a run of a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: The empty theatre sounds like a box office failure, but it is reduced to its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate is to function or run, as a machine works or operates.

blocks.note: OTT is short for over the top
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: A lavish monarch acquires an exotic water creature for the palace.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT, over the top, is informal British for excessive or extravagant.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is a river mammal that swims and hunts fish, so it counts as a water animal.

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: to post a letter is to send it
a tip is a bonus given for good service

explanation.surface: Paying an extra bonus to someone in their job.
explanation.walkthrough: Post looks like a job, but it is the verb meaning to mail; pay is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular salary or allowance, often for clergy or students, so it is a kind of pay.

clue.text: Not able to write and angry about liberal diet

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: irate means angry
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
lite describes reduced-calorie diet products

explanation.surface: A furious person who cannot write is cross about a lenient diet.
explanation.walkthrough: Liberal and diet join first, then the angry word wraps round them; diet is used adjectivally, as in diet cola, matching LITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone illiterate cannot read or write, so the phrase is a plain dictionary gloss.

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the next piece goes behind the one it follows

blocks.note: D is an abbreviation for degree
to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: A student's anxiety about the course they take after graduation.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading a subject is the British way of saying studying it at university.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear or apprehension about something to come, a direct synonym.

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a rat is someone who betrays their friends

explanation.surface: A card sent back to the turncoat who mailed it.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are written backwards as a single string, not separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarot is one of a special pack of cards used in fortune telling, so a single card qualifies.

blocks.note: re means concerning or about
a minder is a personal protector

explanation.surface: An office note concerning a VIP's security detail.
explanation.walkthrough: Minder is British informal for a bodyguard, popularised by the TV series of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: A memo is a short written note to jog someone's memory, which is what a reminder does.

indicators.note: to decapitate is to cut off the head, so the opening letter is removed

blocks.note: an icon is a sacred image of a holy figure

explanation.surface: Examining a statue of a saint whose head has been knocked off.
explanation.walkthrough: Con is an old-fashioned verb meaning to pore over or learn by heart.
explanation.definitionFit: To con a text is an archaic verb sense meaning to examine it closely and learn it.

clue.text: Charlie upset hoarder with empty storage for crack

indicators.note: in a down entry, upsetting tips something so it reads from the bottom upwards
an empty word has lost its contents, keeping only its outer letters

blocks.note: Charlie is the NATO alphabet word for C
a hoarder is one who saves things
first and last letters only

explanation.surface: An agitated hoarder clearing out a storeroom to make room for drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie is also slang for cocaine and crack a form of it, which drives the drug-themed surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevasse is a deep fissure in a glacier or ice sheet, a large crack.

clue.text: Dogs maybe tailing learner in this yarn?

indicators.note: to tail something is to follow behind it, so this piece is placed second

blocks.note: L is the learner driver's plate
the Isle of Dogs is a district of east London, so Dogs is an example of an island

explanation.surface: Dogs chasing a beginner knitter tangled in a ball of yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Dogs is a peninsula in London's Docklands; maybe signals that Dogs is one example of an isle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, smooth cotton thread used for stockings and gloves, so it is a type of yarn.

blocks.note: re means concerning or about
Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective of novels and TV

explanation.surface: A suspect's guilty conscience over the investigating officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is a much-loved British TV detective from Colin Dexter's Oxford novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep regret for a wrong one has done, the sorrowful emotion that goes with guilt.

clue.text: Bit of timber in a solid floor

indicators.note: a bit is a small piece, here just one opening letter
in puts one piece inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
something sound is solid and sturdy
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A plank of wood laid into a sturdy floorboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Floor looks like a noun in a carpentry scene, but it is the verb meaning to stun or knock flat with surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone figuratively is to amaze or stagger them, which is what astound means.

blocks.note: first meaning: a way of tackling a problem
second meaning: a broad street, a place in a town

explanation.walkthrough: Approach reads as a verb, but it is the noun for a method of dealing with something.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue can be a line of inquiry or method, and also a tree-lined street that serves as an address.

blocks.note: up means high or raised
the keep is the main tower of a castle

explanation.surface: The running costs of a castle perched on a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: A keep is the strongest central tower of a castle, so the part stands for the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the cost or process of keeping something in good repair, which is maintenance.

clue.text: Run down lair with one fireplace

blocks.note: a den is an animal's lair
I is the Roman numeral for one
a grate holds the fire in a fireplace

explanation.surface: A shabby, neglected hideout with a single hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: Run down looks like an adjective for a dilapidated lair, but it is the verb meaning to disparage.
explanation.definitionFit: To denigrate someone is to criticise them unfairly or belittle them, which is running them down.

blocks.note: first meaning: to make a picture with a pencil
second meaning: to pull something along

explanation.walkthrough: Two unrelated verbs, one artistic and one physical, share the same four-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: You draw a picture with a pencil, and you draw a cart or curtains by pulling them.

clue.text: Stream of gas upset some homeowners, initially

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so only the leading letter of each word counts

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A gas leak causing alarm among some householders.
explanation.walkthrough: Upset looks like a reversal or anagram signal, but it is just one of the words whose first letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A gush is a sudden rapid outpouring of liquid, a strong stream.

clue.text: Drew together artist, king and journalist

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician
K is king in chess notation
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A painter, a monarch and a reporter sketching together.
explanation.walkthrough: Drew together looks like joint sketching, but it means gathered, as leaves are gathered with a rake.
explanation.definitionFit: To rake leaves or hay is to gather them into a heap, so raked means collected into one place.

clue.text: First part of dinner is hot soup, perhaps

indicators.note: first part means only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: the opening letter
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: The starter at dinner is hot soup.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a menu description; perhaps marks soup as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is any item of food prepared and served as part of a meal, and soup is one such course.

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: averse means opposed or hostile

explanation.surface: Nations that are largely unfriendly.
explanation.walkthrough: States looks like a noun meaning nations, but it is the verb meaning declares.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert or declare firmly, so avers is a formal synonym for states.

clue.text: Short, endlessly short and unwelcome occupants

indicators.note: without an end means the last letter is removed

blocks.note: squat means short and stocky
a terse reply is curt or short

explanation.surface: Brief, abrupt and unwanted residents of a property.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word short is used twice in two different senses: one about height, one about manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Squatters occupy a building without permission or right, so they are uninvited and unwanted residents.
